business_rules.statement: An adoption changes what this blueprint specifies. It never changes what the Statement of Work says, and it never converts a `Recommendation — R&D` into a `SoW Fact`.
The source contradiction stays on the record, in full, with both readings, in its own card.
No adoption may weaken a platform-fixed safety control. Where two readings differ in safety, the safer reading is the one adopted.
No fact is fabricated. Where the resolution requires a fact the source does not contain, the adoption is an interim operating position that avoids inventing it.

Where the source is silent on an SLA, RTO, RPO, retry limit, timeout, queue limit, offline duration, retention period, confidence threshold, model expiry, approval window, or account limit, the register writes `TBD — Client Decision Required`.
Every card names a decision owner and a target date placeholder, because a register with no owner is a list of complaints rather than a plan.
An option set of one is a recommendation wearing a disguise: at least two named options must be described.
A decision is closed only when a test demonstrates the chosen behaviour, not when the meeting ends.
The card is never rewritten to erase the alternative; the alternative is marked *not selected* with the date.
Decision owner is a role, not a person, so ownership survives staff change.
Every card carries all eighteen fields of the register field table, with no blank field.
No card states a contractual value the Statement of Work does not state; every such value reads `TBD — Client Decision Required`.
The sixteen starter taxonomy names appear nowhere in the blueprint.
Exactly five tenant role types, fixed at V1, with custom roles deferred beyond V1; there is no Quality Director role; Job Owner is a field on the Job record, not a role.
Multi-role assignment is additive and the audit log records identity and action, never an 'acting as role' fiction.
Delegation is deferred beyond V1, with cover handled by manually adding and removing the role.
Separation of duties is absolute: the creator of a Job cannot approve it, and the Reviewer must be a different person from the Author, with no role performing two stages on one submission.
At least one Tenant Admin always exists, and an approver-capable role exists whenever a Job exists; attempting to remove the last holder fails with the rule stated.
The root account is created through the backend at platform commissioning, never through any user interface, and is the sole authority for console account creation and role assignment.
Support sessions are read-only, reason-required, ticket-linked, tenant-visible, and terminable by the tenant from the banner.
The compliance-emergency path is the only path with write capability into tenant data and requires two authorisations — the root and one Admin.
business_rules.applies_to: tenant data writes by platform staff

business_rules.statement: No ambient browsing exists anywhere on the platform console; record-level tenant operational content is reached only through exactly three named, audited, session-scoped access classes.
No user interface path exists that creates a second Root Super Admin account.
A support session cannot perform any write into tenant data; attempts are refused and audited.
The permission engine computes authority per role-scope pair until `DEC-PERM-001` is decided otherwise, and logs the computation basis on every denial.
No authority matrix in the delivered blueprint uses '+' notation without an enumerated role set beside it.
The operational hierarchy is Site to Area (Line) to Location (Cell) to Job to Run; depth is the tenant's choice, all levels above Job optional beyond the minimum.
A Site is the facility and the timezone and shift anchor. A Shift belongs to a Site, inheriting its timezone, binds to Areas, and carries its own digest delivery time.
The run record lifecycle is submitted, complete, finished, and the finish is the one automatic transition on the platform.
The Job anchor is stored as a node reference capable of holding any hierarchy level, and the picker exposes every level the tenant configured.
Every tenant has at least one Site from the moment provisioning completes, because a default Site is auto-created there, and no configuration path removes the Site level.
The platform refuses to create two Shifts with overlapping times bound to the same Area, stating the rule.
The tenant-configuration registry rejects a record-finish window outside 24 hours to 7 days with the bound stated in the refusal.
An escalation with no on-shift holder of the target role delivers to the Quality Manager role and is visibly marked as a fallback delivery.

No historical record is rewritten. Evidence and captures are immutable at creation, and corrections are append-only annotation records. A reporting discontinuity is acceptable; a rewritten record is not.
business_rules.enforcement_point: terminal safe state for the hierarchy cluster

business_rules.statement: The Studio approval chain is Author, then Reviewer, then Release Authority; no Workflow content reaches the frontline without explicit human sign-off at each stage, and the Release Authority cannot be bypassed.
A locale-completeness check blocks publication in an incomplete locale.
The Studio cannot publish a workflow containing an input type the Frontline Worker Application does not declare in the screen-element contract.
Every published version record states whether it was created by the human approval chain or by a Lane B automatic publication, and names the approver in both cases.
Every agent record declares its gate type as authoring-time pre-authorised policy or runtime human gate, and the console renders it.
A work package fails validation on the device when a mandatory manifest section is absent, and the run is not marked ready.
A Content Library edit does not alter the content of any run already assigned; the deviation workspace displays the packaged version alongside the current library version.
Terminal safe state for capture types: no screen is publishable whose input type the Frontline Worker Application does not declare support for; publication is blocked with the reason stated.
The command channel carries exactly five classes: lot release, reassignment or substitution, qualification clearance, suspension, and version change, applied at the device's next sync, in order.
There is no real-time remote control of a worker mid-run; captures arrive richly and quickly, commands arrive reliably but eventually, and this asymmetry is stated openly wherever it is user-visible.
Media is evicted only after confirmed server receipt plus an integrity check; remote wipe is server-triggered and every erasure is preceded by a final sync attempt of pending captures.
No Frontline surface displays a single word such as 'synced'; every sync state is reported by its distinct state name and count.
A pending wipe command renders as pending on every surface until the device acknowledges application; no surface implies an offline device applied anything.
Media is never evicted before confirmed server receipt and a passed integrity check, under any storage condition.
A device whose cached credential exceeds the tenant's trust window ceiling locks and refuses new capture until re-authentication.
Under a compliance suspension the device preserves all local data and displays the fixed message verbatim.
No artificial-intelligence model sits in the deviation-triggering path; detection is rule-based and runs on the worker's device, and agents activate only after a deterministic trigger.
The evaluation gate is hard and has no off position for any account including the root.
Every agent record names the model version in force, and every evaluation result is attributable to a model version.
No model reaches production without a complete passing scenario suite, including retrieval evaluations.
Provider unavailability never suppresses the on-device deterministic layer.
Agent unavailability is displayed to tenants as unavailability, never as silence or as normal operation.
A failover target, if configured, has its own passing evaluation record before it can serve traffic.
No agent action can release a Severity 1 hold under any model or failover condition.

The tenant-configuration registry is one console object per tenant holding every tenant setting as three values — the platform default, the bound, and the tenant's current value — and rejects out-of-bound values outright rather than logging them.

Registry changes ride maker-checker: platform-side current-value changes are Admin actions, default changes are engineering class, and bound changes are floor-register changes and therefore critical class.
The tenant detail page displays an effective state for every capability, computed from global, tenant and entitlement states, never blank.
The tenant-configuration registry rejects every out-of-bound value at entry, stating the bound, and never accepts and logs it.
A soft suspension can be lifted by a recorded operator action without any payment integration being present.
The seeded taxonomy ships empty rather than with invented names, until `DEC-TAX-002` is answered.
business_rules.applies_to: seeded Job Type and Service Type catalogues

business_rules.statement: Every suspension-state transition writes tenant state history and is audited, and no transition exists that is not in the enumerated table.
Nothing is purged. The tenant-set retention value, default 15 years, is a hot-retrievability horizon after which data tiers to lower-cost storage and remains retrievable.
Deletion occurs only where a named compliance standard requires it, and the client identifies which standards those are.
Anonymisation is the platform's one irreversible act; switching into Regulated-Industry mode later does not resurrect anonymised identities.
No data is deleted by any automatic process in the absence of a configured, named compliance standard.
A legal hold suspends both tiering and compliance-driven deletion for its scope, and release requires dual approval.
Anonymisation removes the identity link only; measurement, result and evidence remain byte-identical and verifiable.
Regulated-Industry mode tenants never anonymise, and switching into the mode does not restore previously anonymised identities.
No tenant-facing surface or document states an ITAR or EAR posture before `DEC-CERT-001` is answered.
Under the one-transaction guarantee, an action and its audit event commit together, so an occurrence that cannot be audited does not happen.
Every scheduled behaviour on the platform is represented by a schedule definition object with an owner, a timezone anchor, and a declared misfire policy.
No scheduled occurrence executes twice; duplicate execution is prevented by lease and rejected by fencing token.
A scheduled occurrence and its audit event commit in one transaction; an occurrence that cannot be audited does not happen.
Scheduler unavailability never affects on-device gates, specification checks, severity classification, or the Severity 1 hold.
Recurrence generation creates no new runs for a hard-suspended tenant.
Every containment checklist step defined anywhere in this blueprint is fully renderable from the work package with no server call.
No chapter asserts the superseded reading, that the Deviation and Containment Agent triggers the containment checklist, as current product behaviour.
The index lists every card in this chapter, and every card appears exactly once.
No decision in the index is marked resolved while both readings of its contradiction remain live.
No coverage claim anywhere in the blueprint asserts completeness while this index is non-empty.
Every Part XII item appears in section 51.10 with its original grouping preserved; no item is silently merged, split, or resolved.

options: Option A — pre-authorised policy is the gate
Option B — runtime gate always
Option C — per-agent declaration in the governance-binding field (recommended)
decisions.adopted_working_position: Option C, adopted 2026-08-14. Gating is declared per agent in the agent record's governance-binding field; declared values are `authoring-time policy`, `runtime human gate`, and `none — reasoning agent`. Prevention Agent = authoring-time policy; Deviation and Containment Agent = runtime human gate for proposals beyond pre-authorised containment; Shift Handoff Agent and tenant-composed agents = none — reasoning agent.

decisions.question: Capture-upload versus command-download ordering at reconnection
options: Option A — captures first
Option B — commands first
Option C — interleaved by class
decisions.adopted_working_position: Option C, adopted 2026-08-14 because it is the safer reading. Phase one applies the stop class (suspension in all three states, device de-authorisation and remote wipe, any tenant compliance stop) after identity/tenant/device/token/suspension-status validation and before any upload; phase two uploads the full durable queue; phase three applies the enabling class (lot release, reassignment or substitution, qualification clearance, version change).

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A decision passes its target date with no owner response, or an engineer resolves a contradiction silently in code
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The blueprint's stated assumption stands, is re-flagged in the phase report, and the build item is placed behind a feature control
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where no assumption can be safely made — DEC-TAX-002 is the clearest case — the item is not built
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The dependent capability ships disabled, with the seeded catalogue empty and the tenant's own Job Type creation path fully functional
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On receipt of the decision, the capability is enabled through the normal change-approval cycle; overturned assumptions are applied as versioned migrations with audit records

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The role decisions are not made and the build proceeds on assumption
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Implement DEC-PERM-001 Option A (per role-scope pair) and the additive reading of DEC-PLUS-001, both the narrowest safe interpretation
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A tenant's operating model requires a wider reading before the decision lands; no widening is applied
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The narrowest interpretation stands; nothing on the floor stops because the narrow reading never removes a Worker's ability to execute
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Permissions widened by a versioned configuration change through the maker-checker cycle; denials during the assumption period are exported

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A hierarchy decision arrives after tenant data exists under the other reading
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Migrate the affected Jobs by re-anchoring them to the decided level, as an audited configuration change with a per-Job record
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Re-anchoring would orphan historical runs from their reporting grouping; historical grouping preserved and new grouping applies from the migration date forward
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No historical record is rewritten; a reporting discontinuity is acceptable, a rewritten record is not
failures_fallbacks.recovery: New Jobs created under the decided reading; the migration report lists every re-anchored Job; the five standard report sets re-run for the affected period

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The capture-type contract is not agreed and the two workstreams build divergent sets
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Both workstreams build only the five types present in both lists — measurement, scan or barcode, photo, electronic signature or digital signature, and free text
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A launch tenant's workflows require a contested type; the workflow is authored using an available type and the limitation recorded
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No screen is publishable whose input type the Frontline Worker Application does not declare support for; publication blocked with the reason stated
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Remaining types implemented on both sides in one coordinated release with joint evaluation scenarios; no automatic rewriting of published content

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A device reconnects, applies a suspension command, and the worker's unsynced captures are still on the device when the tenant's access is cut
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Under hard suspension the enumerated completion pipeline is protected: in-flight runs complete, capture, sync and close, so upload is permitted
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Under compliance suspension all logins are blocked immediately and devices lock at next contact; unsynced captures on a locked device are stranded
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The device retains the encrypted store and displays 'Operation suspended. Contact your supervisor. Your work has been saved.' Nothing is deleted
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Entry only through the dual-authorised compliance-emergency path; on restoration the device uploads its queue and late captures follow the audited-recompute rule

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The model provider becomes unavailable mid-shift
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Under DEC-MODEL-002 Option B, failover to a pre-approved, evaluation-passed target, audited and visible
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No target available: the emergency pause is invoked per tenant or platform-wide
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Agents unavailable, rendered honestly; raised gates remain human-decidable; the on-device deterministic layer — gates, specification checks, severity classification, and the Severity 1 hold — continues untouched
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Resume is a separate audited act and is critical class; checkpointed agent runs resume or are re-planned

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A global disable is issued for safety reasons and tenants keep executing the capability through pinned packages
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Where the capability is agent-backed, the emergency pause stops it immediately server-side, platform-wide or per tenant
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the capability is packaged deterministic logic, the pause does not reach it; the recall path of DEC-FEAT-006 Option C is the only remaining mechanism and it is critical class
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Runs complete on their pinned packages and no new package carries the capability; exposure is bounded by the record-finish window
failures_fallbacks.recovery: New packages delivered without the capability at the next run assignment; affected runs listable by package version through the per-device package inventory

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A tenant subject to a deletion-mandating standard is onboarded before DEC-DELETE-001 is answered
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The erasure workflow executes an explicit, scoped, dual-controlled request, producing an erasure certificate to both audit trails
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A legal hold in force blocks compliance-driven deletion for its scope; where a hold and a deletion obligation conflict, the hold wins and the conflict is escalated
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Data is retained and the conflict is documented; deleting under uncertainty is not reversible
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On receipt of the standards list, standing triggers configured through the critical-class change path; every tenant onboarded before the list lands is reviewed against it

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The scheduler is unavailable for several hours
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Occurrences apply their per-class misfire policy on recovery
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Backfill would flood recipients; the bounded horizon of DEC-SCHED-004 collapses duplicates and labels the collapsed content
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No scheduled work runs, no duplicate runs, and nothing safety-relevant is affected because specification gates, severity classification and the Severity 1 hold are deterministic and on-device
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The scheduler resumes, each schedule's next occurrence is recomputed, and the misfire record explains the gap

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The client walkthrough does not happen, or happens without the seven items being named
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The seven items are circulated in writing with a response deadline, and the six owed items are chased individually
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where an owed item does not land, the interim position on its card stands and is stated in the phase report as an assumption
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No capability dependent on an unanswered item ships enabled; the taxonomy seeds empty, no export-control claim is made, data sets 4 and 5 are not built
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Each answer applied through the change-approval cycle on receipt; tenants onboarded under an interim position are listed per item

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The decision index drifts from the cards as decisions are made
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The cards are authoritative; the index is regenerated from them
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where a card is missing for an indexed identifier, the identifier is quarantined rather than deleted
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The register is internally consistent or the assembly fails; no blueprint ships with a dangling decision reference
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The missing card is written and the index regenerated; every chapter referencing the quarantined identifier is listed for review
